summary: Generates finite repeating waveform channels with controllable shape, period, phase, amplitude, offset, decay, and range.
key_concepts: Wave CHOP generates finite waveform channels over a specified time range.
The default output is 10 seconds of 1-second sine waves, with repeat extend conditions outside that range.
Wave shape options include constant, sine, Gaussian, triangle, ramp, square, pulse, and expression.
Period, phase, bias, amplitude, offset, decay, and ramp controls shape the generated waveform.
Channel Name supports pattern expansion, so one parameter can generate multiple named channels.
Official docs position LFO CHOP as the successor for endless time-sliced waves and Pattern CHOP for time-independent sample shaping.

key_params.name: wavetype
key_params.note: Wave shape such as constant, sine, triangle, ramp, square, pulse, or expression

key_params.name: ramp
key_params.note: Ramp wave type and ramp slope control

key_params.name: channelname
key_params.note: Output channel names using pattern expansion

key_params.name: defval
key_params.note: Default value for default extend condition

common_gotchas: Wave CHOP is finite by default; its extend conditions repeat outside its range.
Official docs say LFO CHOP supersedes Wave CHOP for endless time-sliced waves.
Pattern CHOP gives more control over time-independent waveform sample shaping.
Audio Oscillator CHOP is better for high-frequency audio-rate repeating waveforms.
Channel Name supports pattern expansion for multiple output channels.
Default output is 10 seconds of 1-second sine waves.
build_relevance: 2021.10000+ finite waveform generation; prefer LFO for endless time-sliced waves
